Result: Test Run Successful. Total tests: 265, Passed: 265, Total time: 38.9582 Seconds. Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s).

gates.name: Run the sample in both roles
gates.reason: build/Test-SampleRoundTrip.ps1 is genuinely Linux-only: its own header states 'Linux-only, and it always was: it signals processes and reads the store with sqlite3', and the script P/Invokes libc's kill(2) via a [LibcSignal] class (DllImport("libc")) and shells out to the sqlite3 CLI to read the outbox table. This host is Windows (PowerShell 7.6.5 on Windows 11); libc is not present and the P/Invoke would fail immediately. The corresponding CI check on the pull request (Linux runner) is where the answer for this gate comes from.

gates.name: Start the workload and the edge, the documented way
gates.detail: Started game-service via `GAME_SERVICE_PORT=8080 npm start` from workloads/game-service, which logged {"listening":{"host":"127.0.0.1","port":8080},"readiness":"healthy"}. Built the edge via `dotnet build workloads/game-edge/SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge --configuration Release` (Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)), then ran it from its own bin directory (workloads/game-edge/SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge/bin/Release/net10.0, not the repo root) via `GameEdge__WorkloadBaseAddress=http://127.0.0.1:8080 ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:5080 ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production dotnet SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge.dll`, which logged 'Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:5080' and 'Application started.'. curl results: GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/livez -> 200 {"status":"healthy"}; GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz -> 200 {"status":"healthy"}; GET http://127.0.0.1:5080/health/live -> 200 {"status":"Healthy","checks":[]}; GET http://127.0.0.1:5080/health/ready -> 200 {"status":"Healthy","checks":[{"name":"game-workload","status":"Healthy"}]}. Both processes were stopped afterward (verified no listeners remained on 8080/5080, only TIME_WAIT remnants of closed connections).

gates.name: Run the replay against the workload
gates.detail: cd workloads/game-service && npx vitest run tests/replay.test.ts -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 11 passed (11). All four named assertions (S5.2/S5.3 dump and transcript byte-identity, S5.7 real OS process, S5.9 save-game transcript entry) passed.

gates.name: Run the replay against the edge
gates.detail: Built GameEdge via `dotnet build workloads/game-edge/SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge --configuration Release` (0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)), then ran `GAME_EDGE_DLL=D:\Dropbox\Projects\SubZeroDev.Platform\workloads\game-edge\SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge\bin\Release\net10.0\SubZeroDev.Platform.GameEdge.dll npx vitest run tests/replay-edge.test.ts` from workloads/game-service. Result: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 2 passed (2) - both S7.8 byte-identity comparisons (dump and transcript) passed with the client addressed at the edge.

gates.name: Migrate the schema to head, the documented way
gates.detail: Brought up Postgres via `docker compose up -d postgres` from workloads/game-service (container game-service-postgres-1 reported healthy via its pg_isready healthcheck within one check interval). Then ran `GAME_SERVICE_DB_SCHEMA=ci_documented_migrate GAME_SERVICE_DB_CONNECTION_STRING=postgresql://game_service:game_service@127.0.0.1:5432/game_service npm run migrate` from workloads/game-service. Output: 'migrated ci_documented_migrate to head'. Exit code 0.

gates.name: Start the workload against the durable store, the documented way
gates.detail: With the compose Postgres running, ran `GAME_SERVICE_PORT=8081 GAME_SERVICE_STORAGE=durable GAME_SERVICE_DB_CONNECTION_STRING=postgresql://game_service:game_service@127.0.0.1:5432/game_service GAME_SERVICE_DB_SCHEMA=ci_documented_durable_start npm start` from workloads/game-service. Log output: {"listening":{"host":"127.0.0.1","port":8081},"readiness":"healthy"}. curl http://127.0.0.1:8081/readyz -> HTTP 200, body {"status":"healthy"}. Process was then stopped. One retry was needed: the first attempt failed with {"code":"ListenerBindFailed","endpoint":{"host":"","port":8081}} because ports 8080 and 8081 were still held by leftover node.exe `tsx src/main.ts` processes (PIDs 30132 and 43928) left running from an earlier, uncleaned verify attempt on this same machine; those two leftover processes were stopped, freeing the ports, and the retry succeeded.

gates.name: Run the one-instance contention proof
gates.detail: cd workloads/game-service && npx vitest run tests/contention-one-instance.test.ts (compose Postgres running) -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 5 passed (5), including S6.1/S6.6 (one winner, one 409) and S6.5 (unreachable store yields 503 never 409, evidenced by the expected 'startup migration attempt failed' stderr line from the deliberately-unreachable-store test case).

gates.name: Run the two-instance contention proof

gates.name: Run the durable replay
gates.detail: cd workloads/game-service && npx vitest run tests/durable-replay.test.ts (compose Postgres running) -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 7 passed (7). S8.2/S8.4 dump byte-identity, S8.3 transcript byte-identity, and S8.6/S8.9 two sequential durable replays with fresh schemas all passed.

gates.name: Run the port-conformance suite
gates.detail: cd workloads/game-service && npx vitest run tests/conformance.test.ts. First attempt (before Postgres was brought up) failed: 'S9 - port conformance > the durable target > S9.1-S9.8: passes the whole conformance suite' with Error: migrateToHead failed for test schema s3_test_38560_1_4dd6d5e1: {"code":"Unreachable"} (1 failed, 6 passed). After `docker compose up -d postgres` was brought up for the migration/durable gates, the suite was re-run and passed fully: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 7 passed (7).
